chunks: What al-Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—reported to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Idris together, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abi Abd Allah عليه السلام, concerning...
In a long hadith, he said:
And regarding a man from whom wind comes out: is he required to perform istinja'? He said: “No.”

And he said: “If a man urinates and nothing other than that comes out from him, then only his penis is upon him to wash, and he does not wash his anus. And if something comes out from his anus and he does not urinate, then only the anus is upon him to wash, and he does not wash the penis.”
And he said: “He is only required to wash what is ظاهر of it, and he is not required to wash its interior.”

key_terms.إِحْلِيلَهُ: his penis; the organ to be washed after urination
key_terms.الرِّيحُ: wind; passing gas that does not require istinja' in this ruling
key_terms.بَاطِنَهَا: its interior; the inner part that is not required to be washed
key_terms.مَا ظَهَرَ: what is outwardly visible; the external area that must be washed
key_terms.مَقْعَدَتَهُ: his anus; the area to be washed after discharge from it
key_terms.يَسْتَنْجِيَ: to perform istinja'; cleansing the private area after excretion

ai.seo_question: Does passing wind require istinja', and what exactly must be washed after urination or defecation?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal ruling for cleansing after minor excretions. It states that passing wind does not require istinja', that urine requires washing the penis only, and that fecal discharge requires washing the anus only, with the obligation limited to the outwardly apparent area.
